_readme: Every roof Josh has pointed at, with what he said and whether it is fixed NOW. Written by tools/cases.py; edit by hand only to correct a quote. A case is never deleted -- a fixed roof that breaks again must be visible as a REGRESSION, not vanish.

cases.defect: truncated pyramid: 4 slopes plus a real 4 m flat square at the peak
quotes: Clearly you have made up a square box on one of the sides of the rectangles
It's the same and still wrong
On the pyramid you are missing the square in the middle at the top. It ends in a square at the peak which should be visible in both imagery and lidar.
notes: verdict on 18 Sep was given against a render made WITHOUT SOLAR_SELECTED_FACES -- the old geometry path, not what ships. Re-rendered correctly for a fresh verdict.

LiDAR 18 Sep: a plateau of cells at 2.32-2.38 m above the eave, ~4 m across, ~0.9 m above the surrounding roof with a sharp step. The flat top is REAL. trunc_hip was right in kind but placed it off-centre (snap_form slid it); the pyramid fix then deleted it. Correct answer: 4 slopes + the square, located from the LiDAR plateau rather than from a guess-grid.

cases.defect: unnecessary inaccurate roof lines drawn where none exist
quotes: You've drawn a bunch of unnecessary inaccurate roof lines here
Very wrong, way too many faces being created and in the wrong places with the wrong roof lines, basically a complete failure
notes: FLAT COMMERCIAL WITH PLANT -- no deep shade at all (0% below luminance 70) and low contrast (sd 27). The line detector polygonises duct and plant edges into roof lines: same failure as #4722059's 85-face web, at smaller scale. Line reading scores 0.58 so the complexity gate does not catch it.

cases.defect: fuzzy, jagged boundaries following nothing visible
quotes: These roof lines are fuzzy, no roof lines are fuzzy, this makes no sense.
A failure adding extra lines and faces that shouldn't be there
notes: MULTI-LEVEL FOOTPRINT -- one outline spanning 10.66 m of height over 167 m2, so the roof is several separate roofs and is read as one. Surface is CLEAN (0.18 m cell spread), so this is not shade; the single-plane inlier of 0.13 is the giveaway. Needs splitting by height level before any form is fitted.

cases.defect: not close to the obvious faces visible in the imagery
quotes: This roof here has gotten much worse. It makes no sense and is not even close to the obvious faces visually
Clearly wrong and nothing like the roof. It is getting confused by shadows.
notes: UNDER TREES -- neither sensor can see this roof. LiDAR top surface is rough at 0.64 m within 1 m cells (a clean roof measures 0.18-0.22) and 20% of its pixels sit below luminance 70. Best plane fit over the whole footprint is 0.15 inlier. Every reading scores 0.37-0.42. Josh: 'getting confused by shadows'. The honest output here is minimal geometry or none, not five fragments.
